[quote=united_hydronia;59728663][b]Diplomacy - A letter to Narrvekk[/b]

[i]To the nation of Narrvekk,[/i]

Greetings, I am Kaplan Zorlu, president of the Democratic Republic of United Hydronia. We wish to establish positive diplomatic relations with your country and have therefore extended an invitation to our capital, Hydropolis, for a representative  of your nation to visit. If you accept, we will expect a letter back and for your representative(s) to arrive at Hydropolis within 2 days.

[i]Yours sincerely, President Kaplan Zorlu[/i]

[nation]Abadi-JR[/nation][/quote]
[i]What is an Hydronia?![/i]
Ka'ak-Duur questioned to the other Ërshuun, one of them, Eren, answered, as he takes the paper to read again.
 [i]This is human writing, so therefore must be something human, this man, Kaplan Zorlu seems to be inviting us for something.[/i]
[i]I see...I am afraid, there is no response we can send in matter of 2 days, would anyone here be willing to go to such "Hydronia"?[/i]
The Zheks(Zhekvekk) present nodded in non-agreement. Ka'ak-Duur sighed, and said.
[i]Y'all so afraid to leave our nation, despite being our habitat, contact with other sapients is also important, prepare the galiot, I will not be willing to swim today.[/i]
[i]Understood sir.[/i]
They all answered in understood, Eren got aboard the galiot alongside the Thrrum-ennak, he wasn't an Ërshuun, yet the heir and apprentice of Ka'ak Duur, despite the cold, which could be deadly to humans, for the Zhekvekk, they were already well adapted. 
[i]I see land, and a blue and orange flag, let's get into this place.[/i]
It was the coast of Yorgul, they didn't know, but would need walk a bit much to reach where they should, quickly Ka'ak-Duur got into the icy waters, his body well adapted to swim, they rapidly managed to get into the coast, with his fangs clashing against the rocks, he got into land, and helped his apprentice, it was night, he looked around, it was all different from his homeland, despite being cold the Zhekvekk wear no cloths as their skin is thick and can project enzymes to protect their bodies from freezing at such temperatures, however they also bought a packet of Esh'gurt to keep hydrated and Khay(tea...?) to present, and a letter in response...?
[i]Now, where is a city named Hydropolis located...? Master?[/i]
The master gave a short glance at his apprentice and said.
[i]I don't know neither.[/i]

[spoiler= Part 3: Chérnagard]Long before the modern borders of Chernarus were drawn, before the dusty flags of post-communist resistance fluttered over Vystok and before gray bureaucrats scrawled decrees in foreign languages, the land was known by another name: Svartháland, the Black Highlands.
It had not been a country then, but a province, the easternmost reach of the First Commonwealth of Jomsland, a land both wild and sacred, a liminal threshold between the known world and the unshaped chaos beyond. Here, in the sweeping meadows and along the jagged eastern coasts, druids once read the wind in the grass and listened for the gods in the howl of wolves.
In the age of Jorik the Boneless, Svartháland was more than a frontier. It was a keystone of the realm, a vital limb of the great beast that was the Commonwealth. The highland clans of the Hjerlendr, once scattered and proud, had bent the knee to the Blodskald bloodline during the Great Pact of Kernågard. It was not submission, it was synthesis. Their warriors fought side-by-side with Jomslandic Úlfhéðnar, bearing axe and oath against raiders from the sun-scorched east and heretic cults from the south.
In those days, Svarthálands loyalty was as deep as its roots. The bones of jarls who died for the White Dragon banner still lie beneath the soil, tucked under strip malls, highways, and the foundations of forgotten Soviet-era factories. Their names have been erased from modern maps, but not from the sagas.
But all was lost with the fall of the First Commonwealth. When Gorm the Lazy slouched on the throne and the dikes broke, when the waters came howling across the land and drowned a thousand farms, the unity of Jomsland fractured. In the chaos of the Age of Fragmentation, Svartháland rebranded itself as Chernarus, not merely in name, but in spirit too.
They embraced foreign ideologies. They threw down the shrines and burned the runes. The true gods were buried under concrete, replaced with cold marble busts of Reason and Progress.Their sagas were rewritten in foreign tongues. their children raised to scorn the ancestors. The bond was not broken. It was betrayed.
To High King Jorik III Blodskald, heir of the dragonblood and restorer of the flame, this was not merely rebellion, it was apostasy. And so, in the year of the return, after victory was sealed with iron and blood, he issued the decree that would shake the gods awake:
The Grand Blót.
They came from every corner of the realm, pilgrims, priests, engineers, skalds, veterans. They marched by torchlight, bearing offerings and ancient banners, to the Grand Temple of Uppsala, the most sacred site in all of Jomsland.
Built atop a volcanic outcrop, the temple had been the blazing heart of the Commonwealths soul. For nine long years since the last Grand Blót, it had lain silent, its altars cold, its fires extinguished out of respect for the gods. But now, under banners of white dragons and amid thunderous war-drums, the mountain stirred once more.
At its center stood the Blót Altar, a large altar forged from meteoric iron and engraved with the names of the gods. Infront of it stood Jorik himself, cloaked in black ceremonial robes, a crown of deer antlers and a deer skull maskhiding his face, embodying both king and priest. Before him knelt ten insurgents, hands bound, heads shaved, marked by red ink: the last of the Vystok resistance.
Among them were generals, propagandists, and university deans, those who had taught the lies of democracy and reason, who had defiled shrines, erased memory, and called it progress. Their deaths were not vengeance, but atonement. One by one, they were led to the altar, their blood spilled across the black stone to feed the gods and cleanse the land.
The skalds sang as the blades rose and fell. Chants filled the air like incense. The priests carved runes into the bones of the fallen and burned them in ritual pyres. As the last heart stopped beating, thunder cracked overhead. A single bolt of lightning struck the distant sea, and the high priest turned skyward, declaring the storm to be divine affirmation.
From that day forward, the territory once known as Chernarus bore a new name:
The Jarldom of Chérnagard.
The name itself was a reclamation, part Slavic, part Jomslandic, a fusion of past and future. It signified not occupation, but transformation. A new Jarl, Bogdan I, was appointed, a grizzled veteran of the old Chernarusian army who had defected early in the war. At the altar, he swore an oath of blood and fire to the Blodskald dynasty.
His first act as Jarl was to declare Vystok once again the capital, not as a defiant holdout, but as the administrative heart of the new order. Before the Althing, the banner of Chérnagard was unveiled: a black wolf on a crimson field. Its message was unmistakable:
The savage made civil. The rebel tamed.
Reconstruction followed quickly. Massive shrines to Wadruna, Varnja, and Nirvold were raised in every major settlement, often atop the ruins of old government buildings. New schools were opened under the Althings Curriculum, which emphasized martial ethics, Jomslandic history, Teutonic literacy, and loyalty to the gods.
The war against resistance became a war for the soul. Dissent was not punished as crime, but as heresy. Apostates were drowned, burned, or sacrificed. Some fled into the eastern mountains to form desperate militias. Others were hunted down by Jomsvikings, tracked like animals through the snows.
Most bent the knee.
And through it all, the world watched in stunned silence, silenced by the fireball at Vetrarhald, cowed by the sheer audacity of an empire resurrecting itself not only through conquest, but through ritual, through memory, through the invocation of forgotten gods.
High King Joriks vision was all but realized. He had not only reclaimed a lost province, he had rewritten it. He had awakened the ancient faith in a people raised in denial. He had brought the Commonwealth into the atomic age, not as a servant of modernity, but as its master.
Now, as Jomsland's borders crept outward like frost across Lake Ilinalta, one truth had crystallized in the hearts of all who looked north:
The Commonwealth had returned.
And this time,  it would not fall.[/spoiler]
